notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #10] Video Tour and Demo coming soon
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

Let's start with an important announcement: [b]this year we'll release the first Demo of Glasshouse on Steam[/b]. Due to circumstances beyond our control, we can't reveal the date yet -- just know that we've almost completed work on ACT I and this demo will be taken directly from a portion of it.

Now comes the most exciting part of development; [b]we're implementing dialogues, assets, and mechanics[/b], and what once seemed like an impossible puzzle to complete is now a wonderful interactive canvas. We want to celebrate GLASSHOUSE's [b]3rd birthday[/b] with a [b]video tour of Dormitory 73B[/b], one of the main settings, now finally connected between almost all its parts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/d1e1b6b5ab46e4cb099e76d84f4b27b1eb1ed25c.gif[/img]

[h2]SHARED SPACES: FROM GROUND FLOOR TO 3RD FLOOR[/h2]
Dormitory 73B consists of [b]four floors and six apartments[/b]; its past as an industrial slaughterhouse has allowed us to build an intricate and unpredictable level design, architecturally 'uncomfortable' and full of [b]secrets to discover[/b]. Each apartment is [b]completely explorable[/b] and directly mirrors the popular culture of the Lundonstoch fiefdom.

[previewyoutube=NYl34ZgMIE4;full][/previewyoutube]
While waiting to reveal more information about the Demo's release date, in the coming months we'll begin to show you in detail all the pillars that make up the definitive GLASSHOUSE experience, from the [b]Combat System[/b] to the [b]Political Compass[/b], including a [b]complete overhaul of the UI[/b] itself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8f01e4c5d1e49e36aa367ee60c585f3b09903d20.gif[/img]

Since the release of the Concept Demo in 2023, we've been working tirelessly for over two years to reach this point -- 2025 is the year when Glasshouse will show itself in its definitive form: [b]new trailer[/b], public demo, press releases, [b]rebranding[/b] (new logo coming!), [b]a series of YouTube Devlogs[/b] and much more awaits you in this new phase of collective development.

In case you're wondering, no, [b]we still haven't found funding[/b] and work continues in our free time as it did in 2022. But as was the case three years ago, the flame that fuels our passion remains strong and with or without a publisher, [b]we will see this through to the end[/b]. That's a promise.

Thank you all, see you next month!

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: [DEV-BLOG #9] Visual Upgrades
notes.content:
Hello flatmates,

I'm Andrea Marinelli, [b]Lead Technical Artist[/b] at [b]FLAT28[/b], and I am temporarily ousting Giacomo to create my first devblog. A techno-junkie one.

Over the past few months, [b]we’ve been focusing heavily on improving the visual side of Glasshouse[/b]. Our goal has been twofold: to define a clear visual identity and to set a benchmark for visual quality—a standard we aim to hit with every environment in the game.

To achieve that, we’ve been moving forward on multiple fronts. On one side, we kept working on new assets and building out the Dormitory 73B scenarios to maintain production momentum. On the other, we explored [b]new pipelines[/b] to speed up development while increasing overall visual fidelity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/83d83d06a493328c7ba9f7498d71942dd224b69d.gif[/img]

[h1]CLEANER EDGES & ROOM BORDERS[/h1]
We’ve [b]reworked the borders of every room[/b] and apartment in Dormitory 73B. The goal was to get a softer, [b]more natural separation between the interior and exterior parts[/b] of the rooms, while staying consistent with the aesthetic we're aiming for. The result feels more polished, cohesive, and true to our vision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/5635922b37ff8dfef08443c5bf541d9268c547c3.gif[/img]

[h1]NEW POST-PROCESSING & OUTLINES[/h1]
One of the changes we're most excited about—and one you’ll likely notice right away—is a new post-processing effect that adds [b]subtle outlines across the entire scene[/b]. (well, might be actually tricky to get it via gif)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/8a7b1b0ab7df3bf241f5757bfd74bc807c44c4e8.gif[/img]

After testing various styles, we landed on an [b]outline shader that felt just right for the tone[/b] and identity of Glasshouse. Both the characters and environments now have a light contour that enhances detail and brings out the uniqueness of our art direction.

From an isometric top-down view, this effect also makes small details more readable, giving players a [b]clearer and sharper sense of space and depth[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7574251189c05e645cd3c7fa583ef1118b82d4c1.gif[/img]

[h1]CLOTH SIMULATION[/h1]
Until now, most of the cloth elements—curtains, drapes, and similar—were entirely static. That’s changing. We’ve begun integrating [b]real-time cloth simulation[/b] for selected elements.

Not all fabrics in the game will be dynamic, due to both performance considerations and artistic direction. But certain curtains and fabrics will now react to player interaction—swaying, shifting, or sliding over characters as they move through them. It’s a [b]small touch, but it adds a sense of life[/b] and responsiveness to the environments.

[h1]DLSS & UPSCALING EXPERIMENTS[/h1]

While it’s still early to talk in-depth about optimization, we’ve started preparing for it. [b]Glasshouse already supports NVIDIA DLSS 3[/b] internally, and we’re exploring dynamic resolution scaling and other upscaling techniques to ensure smooth performance across a wide range of hardware.

That’s all for now—but more is coming. We can’t wait to show you what’s next.

[i]Andrea Marinelli, Lead Technical Artist
FLAT28 Collective[/i]

notes.title: GLASSHOUSE - FAQ #1
notes.content:
Hello flatmates!

In light of recent updates, many questions have arisen about Glasshouse and its future, so we want to take the opportunity to put together a handy FAQ and [b]get ready for 2025[/b], a year that will hold [b]many surprises[/b].

[h1]So, let's get into it![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/3f2958fd6db8b3057e89946da2730d08d2ad32e0.gif[/img]

[u]Q: What is Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Glasshouse is an isometric Turn-Based-CRPG set in a post-capitalist feudalpunk world at the dawn of a terrible world war. Inspired by RPGs such as Disco Elysium and Pathologic, Glasshouse promises an intense narrative-roleplaying experience punctuated by unforgettable characters, complex dialogue trees, multiple endings and deep ideological introspections that go beyond the screen.

[u]Q: What's the Plot of Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] The entire fiefdom is in lockdown when a mysterious triple murder occurs in your apartment building. Unknowingly, you are caught up in a political conspiracy bigger than yourself. Find a way out or find yourself.

[u]Q: Who is the developer FLAT28?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We are an international art collective consisting of 17 members from the film, CGI and video game industries. We have been working on Glasshouse since 2022 in our spare time, without salaries, funding or publishers. Completely smart working.

[u]Q: What's Feudalpunk?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Feudalpunk is a fictional subgenre that mixes elements of the feudal era with contemporary themes or technologies, focusing on social themes such as class struggle and the sharp contrast between them. In Glasshouse's post-capitalist world, following the revolution of 1828, the geopolitical order has overthrown the state model in favour of the democratic feudal model. Inspired by the Kurdish manifesto of Democratic Confederalism, Glasshouse imagines a deglobalised world where technological progress has come to a standstill and the economic-social gap between fiefdoms is unbridgeable, where 100km distance between one fiefdom and another can be equivalent to 100 years of technological difference.

[u]Q: Does Glasshouse have a combat system?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Yes, as announced a few months ago, Glasshouse will have turn-based combat inspired by older Final Fantasy and the more recent Fear & Hunger.

[u]Q: When is the Release Date?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Too early to announce it.

[u]Q: Are you planning an Early Access Release?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] No, no early access release is currently planned.

[u]Q: Are you planning a Kickstarter campaign?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It depends on many factors, first and foremost, the general interest around Glasshouse in these early stages. Kickstarter has changed over time and a proper campaign may require a lot of funding, which we currently do not have.

[u]Q: Will there be voice acting?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] The aim is to have Glasshouse, for the launch, at least with partial voice acting. To date, as there is no publisher, it is difficult to say for sure.

[u]Q: How long will Glasshouse be?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We expect to have a main campaign between 10 and 15 hours. We are a small team (without budget) and want to create a strong, intense and highly replayable experience. For our ambitions, it is necessary to reduce the duration to have an rpg component that really makes a difference. 

[u]Q: Are there any DLC planned?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We have at least one expansion of the main story in mind, but nothing is certain. It will depend a lot on how the development of Glasshouse proceeds and on sales. Let's be clear, we are not talking about cut content, but a possible small additional story that will give another point of view to the main plot.

[u]Q: What is the Concept Demo of Glasshouse?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] A small 3-hour standalone experience from the first 2022 builds of Glasshouse, when we were young and didn't yet know what we were doing. It is a vertical slice mainly designed to sell the settings, atmospheres and core game mechanics to publishers. Nothing included in the concept demo will be present in the final Glasshouse game. You can download it from [url=https://flat28-collective.itch.io/glasshouseconcept]Itch.io[/url].

[u]Q: Why was the Concept Demo removed from Steam?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It was originally conceived in 2022 for pitching to Publishers, and later adapted to a wider audience to gather feedback, experiment and fine-tune our production pipeline. Now, two years later, this version no longer represents the final product and for this reason, we have decided to remove it.

[u]Q: Will the game be available on GOG and other stores?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] It’ll likely be available on GOG and EPIC Store.

[u]Q: Will preorders be available?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] No. ♥♥♥♥ preorders.

[u]Q: What platforms other than PC are planned for release?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] We’re planning releases for PS5 and Xbox S/X, likely following the PC release.

[u]Q: What engine is the game being developed in?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] Unity.

[u]Q: How can I get in touch with the devs?[/u]
[b]A:[/b] You can write us at prj.glasshouse@gmail.com or join our [url=https://discord.gg/HjPTxkfbCw] Discord [/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43329820/7493d54596c091c2cb1ffb076071f102d3eddaed.gif[/img]

That's it for this year, and I want to take this space to make a promise: [b]from 2025 onwards you can expect a devblog every month[/b], with the aim of offering an ever-expanding window on the stormy development journey of the FLAT28 collective. Making video games isn't easy, but damn if it's fun.

We can't wait to reveal [b]the future of Glasshouse[/b] to you.

[i]Giacomo Montagnoli, Creative Director
FLAT28 Collective[/i]
